newsitem.title: UK: Malaysia says reviving cocoa sector.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia says reviving cocoa sector.

text.p: Malaysia has launched a three-year programme to help rehabilitate cocoa farms and improve production to beyond 150,000 tonnes by year 1999, government officials said on Wednesday.

The programme is initially targetted at small farmers who account for the bulk of the country's production, said Annuar Khabar, head of the Malaysian delegation to the International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) meeting in London.
Malaysian output has fallen to around 130,000 to 140,000 tonnes in 1996/97 from a peak of 247,000 in 1989/90 due to prolonged depressed prices, adverse weather and diseases, he told reporters.
The ICCO began a series of committee meetings on Wendesday to prepare for the policy-making council meeting in September. The meetings end on Friday.
Annuar said the sliding production over the years appeared to have been arrested.
The total area under cocoa cultivation will be kept at just over 200,000 hectares after falling from a high of 420,000 hectares in 1990.
Average national yield is around 1.5 tonne per hectare a year. But the majority of small holdings produce just around 0.5 to 0.6 tonnes per hectare, Annuar said.
There has been a declining production from large estates as planters switch to more lucrative crops such as palm oil.
Annuar said current cocoa price of just over 3,000 ringgit per tonne was still unattractive to large plantations.
He said prices should rise to 3,500 or 4,000 ringgit in order to keep people growing cocoa.
